answer: An agent locks a deposit in a shared vault, and the vault dyes it with a unique pigment mark no one can copy or sell. Newcomers take tiny jobs only, and each finished job adds an entry to their voyage log, which graders read before releasing larger work. Caught running duplicate identities, the vault slashes the deposit and wipes the log, so the fake pays and restarts from zero. One fake costs about $1,800, assumed here, so 1,000 fakes cost about $1.8 million, more than they could steal. A vault that dyes every deposit is like a port that paints every hull: copies show at a glance.
